How to Apply: A Guide for International Applicants
We are dedicated to discovering the full essence of who you are and how you will excel within the vibrant academic environment at UTRGV, our tailored application approach is designed specifically for international students.
As an international applicant, you will be required to submit a few supplementary items in addition to the program admission requirements. The steps below outline helpful information and guidance on the application process.
Update On International Admissions From U.S. Immigration And Customs Enforcement
The Student Exchange Visitor Program (SEVP) regulations prohibit the issuance of a Form I-20 based on conditional admission, effective July 13, 2016. University officials can only issue a Form I-20 when students have met all standards for admission for the program of study listed on the Form I-20. These standards for admission include any English proficiency requirements.
Step 1: Fill Out the Online Application
Complete the UTRGV online application at www.utrgv.edu/gradapply.
Review specific admission requirements for your program on the Graduate Programs page.
Pay the application fee online if required.
Step 2: Evaluate Foreign Credentials
Foreign credentials must be evaluated through an approved credential evaluation agency. Choose one of the approved services:
World Education Services (WES)
Foreign Credential Services of America (FCSA)
SPANTRAN
International Education Evaluations (IEE)
Report Type: Select a course-by-course report.
Visit the Foreign Credential Evaluation page for detailed information.
Step 3: Certified English Translation
Translation Needed: Obtain a certified English translation of your educational records.
Official Transcripts must be submitted by the following deadlines:
Fall Admission: October 1
Spring Admission: March 1
Summer 1 Admission: July 8
Deadlines to submit original transcripts (with degree conferred):
Fall Graduation: March 1
Spring Graduation: July 8
Summer I Graduation: August 24
Summer 2 Graduation: October 15
Step 4: Submit English Proficiency Exam Scores
Take one of the accepted tests:
Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL)
International English Language Testing System (IELTS)
Duolingo
Pearson's PTE Academic
Minimum Scores:
TOEFL: 79 Internet-Based, 550 Paper-Based, or 213 Computer-Based
TOEFL Essentials: 8.5
IELTS: 6.5
Duolingo: 105 (Applicants with a score of 105 or above may also be required to participate in a Zoom or Skype interview before receiving a final decision.
Pearson's PTE Academic: 45
For detailed information on exemptions and other important details, visit the English Proficiency Exam page
Step 5: Official Test Scores
Submit official GRE, GMAT, TOEFL, IELTS or other required test scores.
UTRGV codes: GRE - 6570, GMAT – 9P3
Note: Not all programs require an admissions or entrance exam. Review specific admission requirements for your program on the Graduate Programs page.
Step 6: After Applying
Check application status online at www.utrgv.edu/gradapply.
Apply for scholarships or assistantships, if applicable. You can view your funding options on the How to fund my graduate education page.
If you will be pursuing your degree as an *International Student, visit the International Student Services website for more information on submitting the following items:
Financial documentation.
Immigration documents.
Medical Insurance. Required every semester, waivers available for Mexican citizens.
*International Student is defined as someone who is not a U.S. citizen or U.S. resident and has a visa status that allows for study in the United States as a postsecondary student.
Additional Information
Para Estudiantes Mexicanos
Requirements by Country
Para Estudiantes Mexicanos
La Universidad de Texas de El Valle del Río Grande ofrece muchas ventajas para que los ciudadanos mexicanos puedan continuar con sus estudios a nivel de maestría y doctorado. Estamos localizados en el Valle del Río Grande, una de las zonas con menor costo de vida de la región. La familiaridad y cercanía a la frontera hacen de El Valle del Río Grande un lugar en donde se respira un ambiente cálido y una rica tradición cultural.
La Universidad de Texas de El Valle del Río Grande es la universidad pública con uno de los costos de colegiatura más accesibles de Texas. Prueba de ello es el subsidio económico para estudiantes mexicanos (Mexican Tuition Waiver), que le ofrece la oportunidad al ciudadano mexicano de pagar el mismo importe que los residentes de Texas, con lo cual se reduce el costo casi a la mitad.
Para mantener su situación reglamentaria de estudiante internacional en Estados Unidos, el alumno debe estar inscrito en 9 créditos académicos, lo que comúnmente equivale a tres materias. Para ver los costos de colegiatura, visite nuestra página de tarifas de colegiatura.
Además del subsidio económico, existen muchos otros recursos que funcionan en beneficio de los estudiantes mexicanos. Estos son algunos de los enlaces de interés que recomendamos visitar para comenzar con el proceso de admisión a la universidad:
Carreras de posgrado de UTRGV
Oficina de Ingresos Internacionales y Servicios Estudiantiles (ISS)
Los estudiantes de primer ingreso (que hayan terminado la preparatoria) favor de agendar su cita con nuestro departamento de admisiones para licenciaturas.
Para más información de postgrado, llamar al 1-833-887-4842 o escribir por correo electrónico a GradRecruitment@utrgv.edu. Para programar una cita por Teams puede usar este enlace. No dude en ponerse en contacto con nosotros.
Nos orgullece recibir a cientos de estudiantes mexicanos cada semestre. ¡Esperamos que tú también seas uno de ellos!
